meta.title: Yann LeCun's $1B Bet Against LLMs [Part 1]
meta.speakers: Yann LeCun (AMI Labs), Welch Labs narrator
meta.thread_line: 4 threads · why pixel prediction blurs · joint embeddings and collapse · Barlow Twins to DINOv3 · JEPA as a world model

snapshot: Yann LeCun has raised **$1 billion** for JEPA, a non-generative AI framework that predicts embeddings instead of text, pixels or tokens.
LeCun's 2015 "cake slide": self-supervised learning is the cake, supervised the icing, RL the cherry. GPT-1 → ChatGPT later followed that exact recipe.
Generative video prediction fails because a model forced to output one frame averages the possible futures into blur.
Joint embedding sidesteps blur but risks **representation collapse**. Barlow Twins (2021) fixed collapse by pushing the cross-correlation matrix toward identity.
DINOv3 (Aug 2025) reached 88.4% on ImageNet without labels, the first time self-supervised matched supervised.
JEPA = encoders + a predictor of the next state's embedding, optionally conditioned on actions. That makes it a learned world model for planning.
LeCun: LLMs will be replaced "eventually", because agents must predict the consequences of their actions.

themes.title: Self-supervised learning won in language, but next-frame video prediction collapses into blur
themes.lead: Next-token prediction freed AI from labeled data, but the same generative trick fails on video because the space of possible frames is intractable.
bullets: LeCun pioneered convolutional nets in the 1980s. AlexNet (2012) looked uncannily like them and was trained on ~1M labeled ImageNet examples.
Mid-2010s RL renaissance: Google DeepMind on Atari and Go. OpenAI (founded 2015) began with Gym and Universe before Alec Radford and Ilya Sutskever pivoted to Transformers.
**GPT-1** pre-trained on 7,000 books and set new state-of-the-art results on nine benchmarks. GPT-3 (2020) trained on hundreds of billions of examples.
GPT-2 has 50,257 output tokens. A full-HD frame has ~10^15 million possible values, so a video model must output pixel intensities directly.
Ball-bounce example: an LLM keeps separate probabilities per outcome, but a video model predicts their *average*, which compounds into blur when autoregressive.
Key reframing: what matters from pre-training is the internal representation, not the generation.

quote.text: the icing on the cake is supervised learning, and the cherry on the cake is reinforcement learning

themes.title: Joint embeddings fixed blur, then Barlow Twins fixed representation collapse
themes.lead: Mapping two views of the same thing to similar embeddings learns without generating, as long as the network can't cheat by outputting a constant.
bullets: Siamese nets: LeCun's Bell Labs team in the early 1990s detected fraudulent signatures by comparing embedding vectors.
**Representation collapse**: the trivial solution outputs the same vector (e.g. all ones) for every input. Contrastive negatives avoid it, but cost may grow exponentially with dimension.
Stéphane Deny applied Horace Barlow's 1961 redundancy-reduction hypothesis: correlated corresponding neurons, decorrelated everything else. The cross-correlation matrix is pushed toward identity.
Barlow Twins linear probe: 73.2% ImageNet vs AlexNet's 59.3%. Google's 2020 vision transformer reached 88.6% fully supervised.
Follow-ups: VICReg (simplified Barlow Twins) and FAIR Paris's DINO v1–v3.
DINOv3 (Aug 2025) hit 88.4% ImageNet. Its patch embeddings segment a hand, ball, cat or book with no labels.

themes.title: JEPA: predict the next state's embedding, condition on actions, and you have a world model
themes.lead: LeCun's billion-dollar bet is that world models built on joint embeddings are the missing piece of AI, and that they should plan rather than generate.
bullets: 2022 60-page paper "A path towards autonomous machine intelligence": a teenager learns to drive in ~20 hours, while Tesla's millions of hours yield only Level 2.
JEPA predicts embedding(t+1) from embedding(t). The encoder drops unpredictable detail, like leaves moving beside a road in dashcam video.
V-JEPA 2 conditions on robot-arm control signals. Planning searches over actions until the predicted state matches a goal embedding (moving a cup off a platform).
LeCun: this is classical optimal control from the late '50s (USSR) / early '60s (West). What's new is learning the model *and* the abstract state.
Inference becomes a **search**, not autoregressive prediction, which also enables safety guardrails.

quote.text: Initially, they'll solve different problems. Eventually, they'll replace.

takeaways.title: Judge a model by its learned representations, not by what it generates
Track JEPA world models as the planning-first alternative to end-to-end robot policies
Treat AMI Labs' $1B as a bet against the LLM-only consensus, and watch for industrial demos
Read DINOv3 and Barlow Twins to see self-supervised vision catch up with supervised

hot_takes.take: LLMs are really good at manipulating language, but basically nothing else.
Initially, they'll solve different problems. Eventually, they'll replace.
I do not understand how you can even think of building an agentic system without a agentic system having the ability of predicting the consequences of its actions.
LLMs do not have world models.

claims.claim: JEPA world-model approaches will eventually replace LLMs

other_news.title: Sources referenced: LeCun's 2022 position paper, the Barlow Twins and DINOv3 papers, Horace Barlow (1961), and Geoffrey Hinton's related information-content ideas.

glossary.def: Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture: encoders embed input and target, and a predictor predicts the target's embedding.
A joint-embedding network outputting the same vector for every input, trivially maximizing similarity.
Training with positive and negative pairs so different inputs get dissimilar embeddings.
A single trainable layer on a frozen encoder, used to measure representation quality.
A model predicting the next state of the world given the current state and an action.
